gap_title: Quantitative relationship between pore size and fatigue life in L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V under LCF
gap_statement: Although 4 papers report qualitative trends between pore size and Nf in L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V, no study provides a quantitative predictive equation relating pore diameter (in the range 20-200 um) to fatigue life at specific strain amplitudes under LCF conditions. The Murakami sqrt_area model parameters for L-PBF material have not been systematically calibrated.
existing_evidence_summary: 4 papers provide evidence on pore_size -> Nf relationship (LPBF_0003-0006). All show qualitative trends (larger pores reduce life) but no quantitative model.
missing_evidence: No systematic pore size-Nf dataset with controlled pore populations. No Murakami sqrt_area calibration for L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V. No Kitagawa-Takahashi diagram with pore size as defect parameter.
why_it_matters: Without quantitative calibration, Murakami's model cannot be applied to L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V for defect-tolerant design. This gap directly limits the engineering applicability of current literature.
candidate_hypothesis: A Kitagawa-Takahashi diagram can be constructed for L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V with sqrt_area as the defect parameter, with a threshold sqrt_area of approximately 30-50 um below which pores are non-detrimental to HCF life.
possible_equation_or_model: Murakami: Delta_K_th = 3.3 x 10^-3 x (HV+120) x (sqrt_area)^(1/3); Kitagawa-Takahashi diagram
experimental_design: Fabricate 5 specimen sets with controlled pore sizes via L-PBF parameter variation. Characterize by CT. Conduct LCF+HCF tests. Plot results as Kitagawa diagram.
falsification_condition: If no clear threshold sqrt_area emerges from the data, or if the Murakami model overestimates Delta_K_th by >50%

gap_title: Transition mechanism from surface roughness dominance to internal pore dominance in fatigue crack initiation
gap_statement: The competition between surface roughness and internal pores as crack initiation sites is recognized as condition-dependent (roughness dominates at low Delta_K, pores at high Delta_K), but the exact transition boundary (stress level, pore size, roughness combination) has not been experimentally mapped. 5 papers study roughness effects and 4 study pore effects, but only 1 paper directly compares both.
existing_evidence_summary: 5 papers on surface roughness (LPBF_0008-0012), 4 papers on pore size (LPBF_0003-0006), but no systematic cross-comparison.
supporting_evidence_ids: EV_LPBF_0003_0; EV_LPBF_0008_0; EV_LPBF_0009_0; EV_LPBF_0010_0; EV_LPBF_0011_0; EV_LPBF_0012_0
missing_evidence: No controlled experiment with simultaneous variation of surface roughness and pore size. No transition map showing which defect type dominates under which conditions.
why_it_matters: Understanding the transition boundary is essential for: (1) determining when surface post-processing is beneficial vs unnecessary, (2) setting pore size acceptance criteria based on service stress level.
candidate_hypothesis: At stress levels below 60% of yield strength, surface roughness (Ra > 5 um) dominates crack initiation; above 70% of yield strength, internal pores (>50 um) become the primary initiation sites.
possible_equation_or_model: Competition model: initiation_life = min(life_roughness, life_pore); transition at critical stress where life_roughness = life_pore
experimental_design: 2-factor experiment: 3 roughness levels (as-built Ra~15um, machined Ra~3um, polished Ra~0.4um) x 3 pore size distributions (low <30um, medium 30-80um, high 80-150um) = 9 conditions, 3 replicates each = 27 specimens. Test at 4 stress levels.
falsification_condition: If one defect type dominates (>80% of initiation sites) at ALL stress levels regardless of the other defect type

gap_title: Conflicting reports on whether HIP improves or does not affect Paris law exponent m
gap_statement: Some studies report that HIP reduces Paris law exponent m (improving crack growth resistance), while others find minimal change. This conflict may originate from differences in initial defect population, HIP cycle parameters, or testing conditions. The actual effect of HIP on intrinsic crack growth resistance (separate from porosity reduction) remains unclear.
existing_evidence_summary: 2 papers on HIP effects (LPBF_0013-0014) with conflicting conclusions. 6 papers on FCGR/Paris parameters (LPBF_0015-0020) with varying baseline values.
missing_evidence: Controlled experiment isolating HIP effect from microstructural coarsening effect. Paris C and m reported together with confidence intervals. Before/after HIP comparison on same material batch.
why_it_matters: If HIP genuinely reduces m, it provides both immediate (porosity reduction) and long-term (crack growth resistance) benefits. If not, the benefit is limited to pore removal only, affecting cost-benefit analysis for HIP adoption.
candidate_hypothesis: HIP at 920C/100 MPa/2h reduces Paris law exponent m by 0.3-0.5 compared to as-built condition, but this reduction is primarily due to microstructural coarsening (increased alpha lath thickness) rather than pore closure. HIP at lower temperature (850C) achieves similar pore closure without microstructural coarsening.
possible_equation_or_model: Paris law; Hall-Petch type relationship between alpha lath thickness and m
experimental_design: 3 conditions: (1) as-built, (2) standard HIP (920C/100 MPa), (3) low-temp HIP (850C/100 MPa). 10 CT specimens each. FCGR tests at R=0.1. Measure alpha lath thickness by EBSD.
falsification_condition: If m differs by <0.1 between as-built and HIP conditions, or if lower-temperature HIP shows the same m change as standard HIP

gap_title: Lack of near-threshold FCGR data for L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V at multiple stress ratios
gap_statement: Near-threshold fatigue crack growth rate data (da/dN < 10^-6 mm/cycle) for L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V is scarce, especially at stress ratios other than R=0.1. Without this data, the applicability of the Kitagawa-Takahashi diagram and the determination of Delta_K_th for various defect sizes cannot be validated. 6 papers cover Paris regime but only 1-2 extend to near-threshold.
existing_evidence_summary: 6 papers on Delta_K -> da_dN relationship (LPBF_0015-0020). Most focus on Paris regime. Few report Delta_Kth.
supporting_evidence_ids: EV_LPBF_0015_0; EV_LPBF_0016_0; EV_LPBF_0017_0; EV_LPBF_0018_0; EV_LPBF_0019_0; EV_LPBF_0020_0
missing_evidence: da/dN data below 10^-6 mm/cycle at R=0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7. Delta_Kth values with confidence intervals. Crack closure measurements.
why_it_matters: Near-threshold behavior controls the fatigue limit for defect-containing materials. Without this data, Murakami and Kitagawa models cannot be validated for L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V.
candidate_hypothesis: The Delta_Kth for L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V at R=0.1 follows the relationship: Delta_Kth = 5.5 - 2.5 x (sqrt_area)^(1/3)/100, consistent with Murakami's model prediction for HV=350.
possible_equation_or_model: Murakami: Delta_Kth = 3.3 x 10^-3 x (HV+120) x (sqrt_area)^(1/3); NASGRO equation for R-ratio dependence
experimental_design: K-decreasing FCGR tests from da/dN = 10^-5 to 10^-8 mm/cycle at R = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7. 3 replicates per condition. Crack closure measured by compliance method.
falsification_condition: If measured Delta_Kth deviates from Murakami prediction by >30%, or if the R-ratio dependence does not follow NASGRO or Walker trends
